evidence_ids: ledger row_id, document doc_id or fx id 'FX:<date>:<source>:<target>'

duplicate_invoice.meaning: the same invoice (same customer, currency, line items and total) issued and booked twice

fx_conversion.affected_ids: [invoice_id] for invoice postings, [payment_id] for receipt postings
fx_conversion.amount: absolute difference between booked and correct base amount, in base currency
fx_conversion.meaning: a foreign-currency document was converted with a rate other than the policy rate

payment_allocation.amount: remitted amount that should have been applied to that invoice but was not, in payment currency
payment_allocation.meaning: a receipt's remittance (invoice_refs) was not applied, or only partly applied, to an invoice that still had an open balance

period_cutoff.meaning: an invoice dated outside the period was booked in this period

fx.fallback: if no rate is published on that date, use the latest rate dated before it
fx.invoices: AR and revenue are booked at the invoice-date rate
fx.quote: fx.csv rate = units of target_currency per 1 unit of source_currency
fx.rate_date: local date of the source document (invoice issued_at / payment timestamp)
fx.receipts: cash is booked at the payment-date rate; AR is credited at the invoice-date rate; differences go to account 7900

null_convention: missing references are explicit null (JSON null / 'null' in CSV)

period.basis: Business dates are local dates in manifest.timezone. A document belongs to the period iff the local date of its own timestamp (invoice issued_at, payment timestamp) is within [start, end]. Only period documents may be booked in this period's ledger.

receipts.application: A receipt is applied to the invoices in its invoice_refs, each up to that invoice's open balance. Excess over open balances goes to 2200 and may be refunded. Receipts with invoice_refs=null cannot be identified and stay in 2900.
